title: Lower bound characterization of private-coin complexity
statement: Let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ be a function, let $\varepsilon \in \bbr$, and let $R_\varepsilon(f) \in \bbn \cup \{\infty\}$ denote its $\varepsilon$-error private-coin randomized communication complexity, namely the least worst-case number of bits exchanged by any private-coin protocol that computes $f$ with error probability at most $\varepsilon$ on every input. Then for every $n \in \bbn$, the inequality $n \le R_\varepsilon(f)$ holds (in the extended natural numbers) if and only if every private-coin protocol $p$ — over coin tapes $\{0,1\}^{n_X}$ for Alice and $\{0,1\}^{n_Y}$ for Bob, for arbitrary lengths $n_X, n_Y \in \bbn$ — that $\varepsilon$-computes $f$ has communication complexity at least $n$.
hypotheses_covered: n ∈ ℕ, compared in the extended naturals
quantification over all coin-tape lengths n_X, n_Y
quantification over all private-coin protocols p on those coin tapes
replaced:
For any $n \in \mathbb{N}$, we have $n \le R_\varepsilon(f)$ (in $\mathbb{N}_\infty$) if and only if
every private-coin protocol $p$ over coin tapes of any size that $\varepsilon$-approximately
computes $f$ satisfies $n \le p.\mathrm{complexity}$.
